theater: 下薩克森奧斯納布呂克森林

battle.name: 條頓堡森林戰役
battle.theater: 下薩克森奧斯納布呂克森林
battle.brief: 公元9年9月，萊茵河下游行省總督瓦魯斯率三個軍團與兩萬餘輔助兵、騎兵，自威悉河向易北河推進。軍隊在奧斯納布呂克以北的條頓堡森林遭日耳曼聯軍伏擊，縱隊被切斷，瓦魯斯自刎，三面鷹旗盡失。卡面的羅馬重步兵即被困於卡爾克里澤窄脊的那支步兵：重盾與分段鎧甲在沼澤斜坡間無從展開。

kit.name: 羅馬重步兵
kit.history: 分段鎧甲配重盾。羅馬的戰力靠的是補充兵源與補給線，不是靠重裝。

countries: 這場戰爭是羅馬帝國奧古斯都治下萊茵河下游行省總督瓦魯斯率領的羅馬軍，與日耳曼中部多族聯軍在條頓堡森林的一場決戰，時間是公元9年9月。羅馬一方以三個軍團為骨幹：第十七、第十九、第二十二軍團，每團五千至五千五百人，加上二十餘個輔助步兵大隊與數個騎兵大隊，總兵力常被估在兩萬至兩萬五千之間；指揮體系上，瓦魯斯以行省總督兼使節的身分總攬全軍，卡爾維西烏斯·佩多率第十九軍團等部擔任清路的先鋒，卡爾克里澤的戰場就是這條權責線的盡頭。輔助部隊中，巴達維亞與色雷斯大隊久經沙場，騎兵大隊的戰馬與射術是羅馬在密林之外少數可以倚賴的機動力量，但它們必須護住緩慢的車隊與散落的步兵，反而成為最先被切斷的一環。德意志一方則是克魯西里、馬爾西、哈塔提、布魯克特里等部族拼成的聯軍，由曾經在羅馬軍中服役的阿米尼烏斯（阿爾曼努斯）統一指揮；他的父親塞吉梅爾與弟弟英吉奧梅魯斯都是部族首領，馬科曼尼國王馬羅博杜斯也遣部眾參與，但與阿米尼烏斯各懷心思。聯軍沒有常備編制，只靠臨時盟約聚合，計畫以地形與襲擾癱瘓羅馬縱隊，把羅馬軍逐出威悉河、易北河內陸的森林地帶。
countriesEn: This war was a set-piece battle in the Teutoburg Forest, fought in September of the year AD 9, between a Roman army led by Publius Quinctilius Varus, the legate who governed the province of Germania Inferior under the Emperor Augustus, and a coalition of tribes from central Germany. The backbone of the Roman force was three legions, the seventeenth, the nineteenth and the twenty-second, each of five thousand to five thousand five hundred men, together with more than twenty auxiliary infantry cohorts and several auxiliary cavalry alae, for a total usually estimated at between twenty and twenty-five thousand men. In the chain of command, Varus stood at the head as provincial governor and legate, Calvisius Pedo led the nineteenth legion and a flying column in advance to clear the road, and the field at Kalkriese was the end of that line of responsibility. Among the auxiliaries the Batavian and Thracian cohorts were seasoned soldiers, and the cavalry alae, with their horses and their archery, were one of the few kinds of mobile force the Romans could still rely on away from open ground; but they had to cover the slow baggage train and the straggling infantry, and so they were among the first parts of the army to be cut off. On the German side stood a coalition patched together from the Cherusci, Marsi, Chatti, Bructeri and other tribes, commanded in the field by Arminius (Hermann), a Cheruscan nobleman who had served in the Roman army; his father Segimer and his brother Inguiomerus were chiefs in their own right, and Marobodus, king of the Marcomanni, also sent men into the alliance, though he and Arminius had private ends of their own. The coalition had no standing organisation and was held together only by a temporary compact, and its plan was to use the terrain and constant harassment to paralyse the Roman column and drive the Romans out of the forested country between the Weser and the Elbe.
people: 瓦魯斯是這場戰爭的羅馬總指揮，出身羅馬老牌貴族，作為奧古斯都的女婿與外孫入仕，公元6年出任萊茵河下游行省總督，受命把日耳曼中部各族納入羅馬的稅收與徵兵體系，並把徵來的物資與軍械押運回萊茵河。真正毀掉這支軍隊的是阿米尼烏斯：這位克魯西里族貴族在羅馬接受軍事教育，於輔助軍中升到百夫長，熟知羅馬的編制、陣形與行軍紀律，深知羅馬縱隊的弱點正是林地與狹隘地形；他的父親塞吉梅爾、弟弟英吉奧梅魯斯都是部族首領，馬羅博杜斯則是把兵力借給聯盟的馬科曼尼王。佩多是前出清路的將領，率第十九軍團與輔助部隊在戰役第一日被擊退退回；輔助騎兵指揮官普布利烏斯·維特利烏斯在混戰中倖存，後來把所見寫成小冊子，成為今人了解此役細節的重要材料之一。瓦魯斯本人在最後一役陣亡，據說寧可以劍自刺也不願被俘，頭顱隨後被斬下送給阿米尼烏斯。皇帝奧古斯都聞訊震驚，史家記載他反覆以頭撞壁、長夜在宮室間徘徊；至於戰役的經過細節，主要靠塔西陀在《編年史》第一卷裡的敘述留傳下來。
peopleEn: The Roman commander in this war was Varus, a member of one of Rome's old patrician families, who had entered public life as the son-in-law and grandson of the Emperor Augustus and was appointed governor of the province of Germania Inferior in AD 6. He was charged with bringing the tribes of central Germany into the Roman system of taxation and recruitment, and with carrying the tribute and the military stores thus gathered back to the Rhine. The man who destroyed his army was Arminius: a Cheruscan nobleman who had been trained in Roman service, risen to centurion in the auxiliary forces, and had learned the Roman system of organisation, formation and march discipline at first hand, so that he knew precisely where the Roman column was weakest, namely in wooded country and in narrow defiles. His father Segimer and his brother Inguiomerus were tribal chiefs, while Marobodus was the king of the Marcomanni who lent men to the alliance. Pedo was the general sent ahead to clear the road; leading the nineteenth legion and the auxiliaries, he was beaten back on the first day of the fighting. Publius Vitellius, who commanded the auxiliary cavalry, survived the fighting and later wrote a short account of what he had seen, one of the important pieces of evidence for the details of the battle. Varus himself was killed in the last day of the fighting, and it is said that he stabbed himself with his own sword rather than be taken alive, his head afterwards being cut off and carried to Arminius. The Emperor Augustus was badly shaken by the news; the historians record him beating his head against the wall and walking about the palace at night. The details of the fighting itself come down to us chiefly through the account Tacitus gives in the first book of his Annals.
kits: 卡面上的羅馬重步兵代表的是帝國早期的軍團步兵，裝束在公元9年仍然可靠：分段式鎧甲由交錯的鐵片與皮帶扣合，胸前與肩部的加強片可擋住大部分投射物；大型弧面重盾高約一米，弧度配合密集陣形；長矛配重矛桿可擲出二十至三十步；短劍用於最後的貼身格鬥，匕首別在腰側；頭盔多用「元帥型」與「G型」鐵盔，羅馬靴以釘底釘在地面。軍團的骨架是軍旗與鷹旗，由鷹手與持號手護持，丟旗即等於全軍潰散，這正是本役最慘重的損失。輔助步兵用圓盾，輔助騎兵用長劍與大盾，軍團另配弩炮與投石器。本役真正的戰場在裝備對比：日耳曼步兵大多無甲，用木矛、短刀與橢圓形小盾，騎兵以投槍與短劍作戰，靠林地隱蔽與地形分割取勝；羅馬的優勢裝備恰恰需要開闊地與完整縱隊才能發揮，一旦縱隊被切斷，鋼鐵與盾牌就只剩下累贅。
kitsEn: The Roman legionary on the card stands for the infantry of the early imperial army, and his equipment was still serviceable in AD 9: the lorica segmentata was built from overlapping iron plates laced to leather, with extra plates over the chest and shoulders that turned most missiles; the large curved scutum stood about a metre high and its curve was made to work with the close-order formation; the pilum could be thrown twenty or thirty paces, its shaft weighted so that it would drive deep into a wooden shield; the gladius was the last-resort close combat arm, the pugio was worn at the belt, the helmet was usually of the Imperial type or the later G type, and the caligae were nailed to the sole for footing. The framework of a legion was its standards, the signa and above them the aquila, carried by the aquilifer and the cornicen; to lose the standards was to see the army disintegrate, and that was the heaviest loss of this battle. Auxiliary infantry carried round shields, auxiliary cavalry the long spatha and the large shield, and the legions had their ballistae and artillery as well. The real battleground of this war lay in the comparison of equipment: most German infantry were unarmoured, fighting with wooden spears, short knives and small oval shields, while their horsemen used javelins and short swords and won by using the cover of the woods and by splitting the enemy line with the ground itself. The Roman advantage in equipment depended on open country and on an unbroken column; once the column was cut, the iron and the shields became nothing but weight.
tactics: 阿米尼烏斯的戰法完全以羅馬的弱點為目標。他選擇兩側是陡坡與沼澤、中間只容一條道路的狹隘地帶，事先伐倒樹木、堆積土石堵塞道路，再以步兵封住出口，把羅馬縱隊切成數段。羅馬行軍縱隊前段是執旗的先鋒與先導大隊，中段是三個軍團，後段是輔助兵與數百輛載著糧秣、武器與攻城器材的牛車，最慢的部分因此先挨打。佩多前出清路失敗後，瓦魯斯在林邊宿營，日耳曼聯軍夜間切斷通往溪水的道路，羅軍次日被迫在缺水狀態下行軍，士氣與體力一同下降。最後一日，羅軍在卡爾克里澤一帶被壓上一道夾在斜坡與沼澤之間的窄脊，輔助騎兵與車隊全失，軍團被壓縮到無法展開盾陣的寬度；塔西陀記載羅軍曾派身著祭司禮服的使者在陣前求和，仍被日耳曼人殺死，說明聯軍並不打算接受投降。羅軍最後的抵抗是把盾牌相互疊壓成一道壁，據地死守，但既無騎兵掩護也無縱深，終被前後夾擊瓦解。
tacticsEn: Arminius's plan was aimed squarely at the weakness of the Roman army. He chose a narrow defile where steep slopes and marsh closed in on either side and left room for a single road, felled trees and piled earth and stones to block that road in advance, and closed the exits with infantry, so that the Roman column was cut into several segments. The Roman marching order put the standards and the leading cohorts in front, the three legions in the middle, and the auxiliaries with several hundred ox-waggons carrying grain, weapons and siege equipment at the rear, so that the slowest part of the army was the first to be hit. After Pedo's advance guard was beaten back, Varus camped at the edge of the wood, and the German coalition cut the road to the running water during the night, so that the Romans had to march the next day short of water, with the men's morale and strength falling together. On the last day the Romans were pressed up onto a narrow ridge between slope and marsh at Kalkriese; the auxiliary cavalry and the baggage train were lost entirely, and the legions were compressed to a width in which a shield wall could not be formed. Tacitus records that the Romans sent men forward in the dress of priests to ask for terms, and that these were killed by the Germans, which shows that the coalition had no intention of accepting a surrender. The last Roman resistance was to lock shields together into a single wall and hold the ground, but with neither cavalry cover nor any depth behind them, the wall was broken and overwhelmed from front and rear.
data: 可據以寫的數字大致如下。羅軍總兵力常被估為兩萬至兩萬五千人，其中三個軍團合計約一萬五千至一萬七千名軍團步兵，輔助步兵約九千至一萬二千人，騎兵約三千至五千人。戰役橫跨三日：第一日佩多率第十九軍團及輔助部隊前出失利；當日瓦魯斯宿營並遭斷水；最後一日全軍覆沒。塔西陀說退回者寥寥、且多被賣為奴隸，另有數百人逃往北方投奔哈塔提人，多數史家因此認為生還者不足三千，甚至只有數百人。羅軍陣亡約兩萬人，瓦魯斯與數名高級將官盡死，三面鷹旗全部遺失；德意志尼庫斯於公元15至16年取回三面中的兩面，第三面直到公元41年克勞狄即位後才再度出現在羅馬的官方說法裡。日耳曼方面的兵力沒有可靠記錄，聯軍人數可能在一萬五千至兩萬之間，但多數戰鬥屬襲擾與圍困，自身損失應在數千人以下。戰場在今德國下薩克森州奧斯納布呂克以北約十六公里，羅軍自威悉河畔的奧斯特瓦爾德營地向東北推進，最後一日的行程估計不足二十公里。
dataEn: The figures that can be given on good authority are roughly these. The Roman army is usually estimated at twenty to twenty-five thousand men, of whom the three legions accounted for some fifteen to seventeen thousand legionaries, the auxiliary infantry for about nine to twelve thousand, and the cavalry for three to five thousand. The action ran across three days: on the first Pedo led the nineteenth legion and auxiliaries forward and was beaten back; that night Varus camped and the water supply was cut; on the last day the army was destroyed. Tacitus says that those who came back were few and were mostly sold into slavery, while a few hundred more escaped north to the Chatti, and most historians therefore put the survivors at fewer than three thousand, some at only a few hundred. Around twenty thousand Romans were killed, Varus and several senior officers among them, and all three legionary eagles were lost; Germanicus recovered two of the three in AD 15 to 16, and the third only reappeared in the official Roman account after the accession of Claudius in AD 41. No reliable figure survives for the size of the German coalition, which may have numbered fifteen to twenty thousand, but since much of the fighting was harassment and blockade their own losses were probably in the low thousands. The battlefield lies about sixteen kilometres north of Osnabrück in what is now Lower Saxony; the Romans had marched north-east from the camp at Osterwald on the Weser, and their movement on the final day is estimated at less than twenty kilometres.
cause: 這場戰爭並非偶然的遭遇，而是羅馬在萊茵河東岸的整體政策與日耳曼中部社會的衝突攤牌。奧古斯都先後派德魯蘇斯與提比略出兵易北河、威悉河一帶，公元1年受降並安置的日耳曼「王國」只是稅源與徵兵池；瓦魯斯接任後要做的，是把這些部落納入帝國的戶籍、稅賦與兵役制度，並在奧斯納布呂克、奧斯特瓦爾德一帶設立常設駐軍與軍用道路。森林地帶的道路狹窄，一次兩萬人的行動只能靠一條路維持，而這條路正是聯軍可以設伏的地形。德意志貴族不肯長期繳稅與提供兵源；受過羅馬訓練的人更清楚，只要把羅軍引入沒有縱深的林地，裝備精良的軍團也會變成孤立無援的縱隊，而羅馬在德意志內陸既無可靠的盟友哨所，也無就地補給。因此阻止羅馬把這片森林納入版圖，就是維持部族自主的關鍵。
causeEn: This war was not an accidental encounter but the collision of the whole Roman policy on the eastern bank of the Rhine with the society of central Germany. Augustus had sent Drusus and Tiberius out against the Elbe and the Weser in turn, and the German kingdom settled and installed in AD 1 was in truth no more than a pool of tribute and recruits. What Varus was charged with was to fold those tribes into the Roman system of registers, taxes and military service, and to establish permanent garrisons and military roads around Osnabrück and Osterwald. The roads through the forest country were narrow, and an army of twenty thousand could only be sustained along a single line, and that single line was exactly the ground where the coalition could stage its ambush. The German nobility would not pay tribute and provide troops for long; and those who had been trained by the Romans understood well that once the Roman army was led into forest country without depth, even a well-equipped legion became an isolated column, while inside Germania the Romans had neither reliable allied posts nor any local supply. To keep the forest out of the Roman province was therefore the condition of keeping tribal independence.
impact: 這是帝國早期羅馬軍隊最大的一次單次損失，約兩萬人的死傷，相當於萊茵河方面兵力的近三分之一。奧古斯都的對策不是再戰，而是改弦：公元9年後羅軍放棄威悉河與易北河內陸的據點，把前線固定在萊茵河一線，並把徵自德意志的輔助軍與稅源重新編排。帝國此後轉向守成的「安寧」政策，接下來數十年在歐洲大陸不再有大型征服，直到圖密善於公元85至93年重啟德意志戰役。另一面是榮譽上的傷口：三面鷹旗失落，成為帝國記憶中最鮮明的恥辱，直到德意志尼庫斯於公元15至16年取回部分軍旗並焚毀日耳曼聚落，才算勉強找回一些面子。瓦魯斯之死也讓奧古斯都的遺囑與對外政策明顯收斂，萊茵河成為此後四百年的帝國北界，德意志中部則長期處於羅馬的版圖之外，只以貢賦、盟邦與僱傭兵的形式與帝國往來。考古上，奧斯納布呂克以北的卡爾克里澤戰場自十六世紀起被辨認，戰場的掘出物與屍骨檢驗，使這場戰役成為歐亞大陸考古最著名的一戰。
impactEn: This was the single largest loss the Roman army of the early empire ever suffered, around twenty thousand men dead, close to a third of the Roman strength on the Rhine. Augustus's answer was not to fight again but to change course: after AD 9 the Romans gave up their inland bases on the Weser and the Elbe, fixed the front on the Rhine itself, and reorganised the Germanic auxiliaries and the tribute that had been assessed. The empire then turned to a policy of quiet and of holding what it had, and for the next several decades it undertook no great conquest on the continent until Domitian reopened the German war in AD 85 to 93. The other side of the wound was one of honour: the loss of the three eagles became the sharpest humiliation in the memory of the empire, and only the recovery of part of the standards by Germanicus in AD 15 to 16, together with the burning of German settlements, brought back some of the face of Rome. The death of Varus also tightened Augustus's will and his external policy, and the Rhine became the empire's northern frontier for the next four hundred years, while central Germany remained outside the Roman province for a long time and kept in contact with the empire only through tribute, client kings and hired soldiers. Archaeologically, the battlefield at Kalkriese, north of Osnabrück, has been identified since the sixteenth century, and the excavated finds and the examination of human remains have made this battle the most famous single battle site in Eurasian archaeology.
result: 結果是羅軍全滅、羅馬退回萊茵河。瓦魯斯與佩多等高級將官陣亡，三面鷹旗與各團軍旗落入日耳曼聯軍之手，阿米尼烏斯把瓦魯斯的頭顱與其他首領的頭顱一起送到各部族面前展示，把俘獲的羅馬兵與繳獲的軍械分給參戰部族，殘餘被俘者被當作奴隸出賣。聯軍沒有乘勝追擊萊茵河：馬羅博杜斯與阿米尼烏斯之間的嫌隙、聯軍各部的利益分歧，以及缺乏渡河器械與攻城經驗，都使進一步的進攻無法成立，羅馬因此得到喘息並得以重建軍隊。對羅馬而言，此役是征服德意志計畫的終結與萊茵河防線的開端；對阿米尼烏斯而言，它是以聯軍旗幟擊敗皇帝全軍的空前勝利，確立了他在克魯西里與其他部族的權威，也讓他成為北方民族記憶中最鮮明的人物。德意志尼庫斯於公元15至16年的報復性遠征取回部分鷹旗、焚毀多處聚落，但沒有改變河界線；此後羅馬再未組織過同等規模的德意志遠征，直到圖密善時代才重新把戰線推過萊茵河。
resultEn: The result was the destruction of the Roman army and the withdrawal of Rome to the Rhine. Varus and Pedo and other senior officers were killed, the three eagles and the standards of the legions fell into the hands of the German coalition, Arminius carried the head of Varus and the heads of the other chiefs before the assembled tribes, divided the captured Roman soldiers and the booty among the contingents that had taken part, and the rest of the prisoners were sold as slaves. The coalition did not press on to the Rhine: the friction between Marobodus and Arminius, the divergent interests of the tribes that made up the alliance, and the lack of river-crossing equipment and any experience of siege work all combined to make a further offensive impossible, and Rome was given the breathing space it needed to rebuild. For Rome the battle was the end of the plan to conquer Germania and the beginning of a defended Rhine line; for Arminius it was an unprecedented victory in which a tribal coalition destroyed the field army of an emperor, and it confirmed his authority among the Cherusci and the other tribes, while making him the most vivid figure in the memory of the northern peoples. Germanicus's punitive expedition of AD 15 to 16 recovered part of the eagles and burned several German settlements, but it did not move the river frontier; and Rome never mounted another German campaign of comparable scale until Domitian's reign pushed the line beyond the Rhine once more.
